article.title: マンション ≠ mansión
article.part: Contraste Guatemala–Japón — グアテマラと日本語の対照
article.chapter: Préstamos engañosos y equivalencias falsas — 紛らわしい外来語・偽の対応

claims.summary: In Japanese residential usage, マンション means a medium- or high-rise multi-unit residence, usually for sale; its residential sense differs from the English gloss mansion.

Irodori describes マンション as a relatively large reinforced-concrete complex with units for purchase or rent, and アパート as typically smaller, often two to three floors, fewer units, often wooden, generally rented and perceived as cheaper.
Irodori explicitly cautions that Japanese law does not draw a clear distinction between マンション and アパート; the traits presented are typical guide-level descriptions, not hard rules.

Spanish explanatory glosses such as apartment building, apartment or condominium are selected by whether the text refers to the building or an individual unit and do not claim a perfect match between Guatemalan and Japanese property categories.

locator.description: コトバンク, 小学館「デジタル大辞泉」, lines 16–23: マンション is a medium/high-rise multi-unit residence, usually for sale, with 大邸宅 as the source gloss; 精選版 lines 27–33 and 日本大百科全書 lines 35–43.

links.notes: The contrast is stated as Japanese residential meaning versus source gloss, not as a complete English-dictionary definition.

locator.description: 国際交流基金『いろどり 生活の日本語 入門 第7課: 部屋が4つあります』, PDF p. 30 (printed L7-31), lines 1808–1819: reinforced-concrete and relative size for マンション; relative size, 2–3 floors, few units, often wood, rent and lower-cost impression for アパート.

links.notes: Every feature is attributed to the teaching material and phrased as a typical profile.

links.notes: Retains the source’s caveat and avoids a rigid commercial rule.
